questions.stem: All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum (3 x 10^8 m/s). A gamma ray has a frequency of 3 x 10^20 Hz. What is its wavelength?
questions.explanation: Wavelength = v / f = (3 x 10^8) / (3 x 10^20) = 1 x 10^-12 m. This is a picometre, typical for gamma rays. Option B reverses the sign of the power. Option C multiplies instead of dividing. Gamma rays have the shortest wavelengths and highest frequencies in the EM spectrum.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly lists electromagnetic waves in order of increasing wavelength?

options.text: Radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays
Gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, microwaves, radio waves
Gamma rays, ultraviolet, X-rays, visible light, infrared, radio waves, microwaves
Radio waves, infrared, visible light, microwaves, ultraviolet, gamma rays, X-rays

questions.explanation: The correct order from shortest to longest wavelength (increasing wavelength) is: gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, microwaves, radio waves. Option A lists them in order of decreasing wavelength (the reverse). Options C and D have types in the wrong positions. A useful mnemonic is 'Grumpy X-ray Ultraviolet Visitors Irritate Most Rabbits'.

questions.stem: What do all electromagnetic waves have in common?

options.text: They all have the same wavelength
They are all transverse waves that travel at the speed of light in a vacuum
They all require a medium to travel through
They all have the same frequency

questions.explanation: All EM waves are transverse waves that travel at 3 x 10^8 m/s in a vacuum. They differ in wavelength and frequency but share the same speed. Option A is wrong — they have very different wavelengths. Option C is wrong — EM waves do NOT need a medium (unlike sound). Option D is wrong — each type has a different frequency range.

questions.stem: A doctor needs to examine a patient's broken bone. Which type of electromagnetic radiation would be most appropriate?

options.text: Radio waves, because they can penetrate the body
Infrared, because it shows heat from the injury
X-rays, because they pass through soft tissue but are absorbed by bone
Gamma rays, because they have the most energy

questions.explanation: X-rays pass through soft tissue but are absorbed by dense bone, creating a shadow image on a detector. This makes them ideal for detecting fractures. While gamma rays (option D) are more energetic, they pass through almost everything and are harder to use for imaging bones. Infrared (option B) only detects surface heat, not internal structures.

questions.stem: As you move from radio waves to gamma rays across the electromagnetic spectrum, what happens to the energy carried by each photon?

options.text: Energy decreases as wavelength decreases
Energy stays the same — all EM waves carry equal energy
Energy increases as frequency increases
Energy increases as wavelength increases

questions.explanation: Photon energy is directly proportional to frequency (E = hf, where h is Planck's constant). Moving from radio to gamma, frequency increases, so energy per photon increases. This is why gamma rays and X-rays are more dangerous than radio waves — each photon carries enough energy to ionise atoms and damage cells. Option A contradicts the physics, and option B ignores the fundamental relationship between frequency and energy.
